title: Ledger Service
description: Request throughput and errors, ledger operation rates and latency, and outbox health. Functional rather than decorative: every panel answers a question someone asks during an incident.

panels.title: HTTP request rate
panels.description: Requests per second by route and status. The first thing to look at: is traffic arriving at all.

panels.title: HTTP error rate
panels.description: Share of responses that are 5xx. Client errors are excluded deliberately: a 422 for insufficient funds is the system working, and counting it here would make the error rate a measure of how often customers overspend.

panels.title: HTTP latency (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: Percentiles from the request duration histogram. The median tells you what is normal; the tail tells you what is breaking.

panels.title: Ledger transaction rate
panels.description: Successful ledger operations per second by kind. This is the business signal: if it goes to zero while HTTP traffic continues, money has stopped moving.

panels.title: Ledger failures by reason
panels.description: Refusals per second, broken down by cause. A rise in insufficient_funds is customer behaviour; a rise in conflict or error is usually ours.

panels.title: Ledger operation latency (p95)
panels.description: Includes time spent waiting for account row locks, which is where contention on a hot account shows up first.

panels.title: Database connections in use
panels.description: From the .NET connection pool counters. A pool at its limit looks like slowness everywhere else.

panels.title: Process memory and GC heap
panels.description: Runtime instrumentation. Present so that a slow endpoint can be told apart from a process under memory pressure.
